**Subject: Grant Application – Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) for Sacramento Stockton Blvd Community Safety**

Dear Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant Committee,

Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) is a minority-owned social enterprise dedicated to addressing critical gun safety needs within Sacramento's communities of color. These neighborhoods disproportionately experience gun-related incidents, often due to gaps in safe storage, handling, and de-escalation knowledge. Our mission is to empower residents, particularly youth, with life-saving knowledge in a culturally relevant and accessible manner.

Our innovative programs include "Gloxsie 21," a captivating cartoon IP designed to teach gun safety principles to young audiences. We also offer crucial "AI education" to equip community members with future-forward skills, fostering critical thinking and digital literacy alongside safety awareness. Complementing these, our direct "community workshops," hosted in partnership with the Church of Legacy, provide hands-on training on safe gun practices, responsible ownership, and violence prevention.

Funding from the Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant will enable GAFC to significantly expand these initiatives. We anticipate increased gun safety literacy, reduced accidental firearm-related injuries, and greater community empowerment. Outcomes include measurable increases in safe storage and improved conflict resolution, fostering safer environments for families.

GAFC is uniquely qualified by our deep community roots and culturally sensitive approach. As a minority-owned organization, we build trust where traditional outreach often fails. Our partnership with the respected Church of Legacy amplifies our reach and impact, ensuring authentic resonance. We request $15,000-$25,000 to scale our programs.

Thank you for considering our application to foster a safer, more informed Sacramento.
